title: State and Reducers
summary: useState, why updates must be immutable, and reducers with discriminated-union actions.

steps.title: State
body: **Props** come from the parent. **State** is data a component owns and changes over time:
```tsx
function Counter() {
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);          // a value and a setter
return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Clicked {count} times</button>;

Calling `setCount` schedules a re-render: React calls `Counter()` again and `count` has the new value. React decides whether anything changed with `Object.is(old, new)`, essentially `===`. So for objects and arrays:
```tsx
const [todos, setTodos] = useState<Todo[]>([]);
todos.push(newTodo); setTodos(todos);          // same array: React sees no change. Bug.
setTodos([...todos, newTodo]);                 // new array: re-renders. Correct.
setTodos(prev => [...prev, newTodo]);          // updater form: safest when updates queue up
Everything from module 3's immutability lesson is exactly what React needs.

steps.prompt: Why does `items.sort(); setItems(items);` fail to update the screen?
options: `sort` mutates the same array, so the new state `===` the old one and React skips the render
`setItems` only accepts new arrays created with `new Array`

steps.title: Reducers
body: When state has several fields and many ways to change, put all the changes in one **reducer**: a pure function `(state, action) => newState`. Actions are a discriminated union:
```ts
type State = { items: string[]; filter: string };
type Action =
| { type: "add"; item: string }
| { type: "remove"; index: number }
| { type: "setFilter"; filter: string };
function reducer(state: State, action: Action): State {
switch (action.type) {
case "add":       return { ...state, items: [...state.items, action.item] };
case "remove":    return { ...state, items: state.items.filter((_, i) => i !== action.index) };
case "setFilter": return { ...state, filter: action.filter };

In a component: `const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, initial); dispatch({ type: "add", item: "tea" })`. The reducer has no React in it at all, so you test it like any function. Redux works the same way.
Reducer rules: **pure** (no fetch, no `Date.now()`, no random), **never mutate** `state`, and return the **same** state object when nothing changes.

code: type S = { n: number; log: string[] };
function reducer(s: S, a: A): S {
const s1 = [{ type: "inc" }, { type: "noop" }, { type: "inc" }].reduce((s, a) => reducer(s, a as A), s0);
console.log(s1.n, s1.log.join(","), s0.n, reducer(s1, { type: "noop" }) === s1);
steps.explain: Replaying actions through `reduce` is exactly what a reducer is named after. `s0` never changes, and a no-op returns the same object so React can skip rendering.

items: `return state` for an action that changes nothing
steps.explain: Randomness, time and network calls belong outside: pass ids and timestamps in the action instead.

steps.title: A cart reducer
prompt: type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
| { type: "add"; sku: string }              // qty + 1, or a new line with qty 1
| { type: "remove"; sku: string }           // removes the line
| { type: "setQty"; sku: string; qty: number }  // qty <= 0 removes the line
Never mutate. Return the **same** state when `remove`/`setQty` target a sku that is not in the cart.
starter: type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
function cartReducer(state: CartState, action: CartAction): CartState {
solution: type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
function cartReducer(state: CartState, action: CartAction): CartState {
if (action.qty <= 0) return { lines: state.lines.filter(l => l.sku !== action.sku) };
return { lines: state.lines.map(l => (l.sku === action.sku ? { ...l, qty: action.qty } : l)) };
template: {{CODE}}
const dojoS0 = Object.freeze({ lines: Object.freeze([Object.freeze({ sku: "tea", qty: 1 })]) }) as CartState;
let dojoS = dojoS0;
try {
dojoS = cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "add", sku: "tea" });
dojoS = cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "add", sku: "cake" });
Dojo.eq("add twice", [{ sku: "tea", qty: 2 }, { sku: "cake", qty: 1 }], dojoS.lines);
Dojo.eq("setQty", [{ sku: "tea", qty: 5 }, { sku: "cake", qty: 1 }], cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "setQty", sku: "tea", qty: 5 }).lines);
Dojo.eq("setQty 0 removes", [{ sku: "cake", qty: 1 }], cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "setQty", sku: "tea", qty: 0 }).lines);
Dojo.eq("remove", [{ sku: "tea", qty: 2 }], cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "remove", sku: "cake" }).lines);
Dojo.check("remove unknown returns same state", cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "remove", sku: "x" }) === dojoS, "expected the same state object");
Dojo.check("setQty unknown returns same state", cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "setQty", sku: "x", qty: 3 }) === dojoS, "expected the same state object");
Dojo.eq("clear", [], cartReducer(dojoS, { type: "clear" }).lines);
Dojo.eq("original state untouched", [{ sku: "tea", qty: 1 }], dojoS0.lines);
} catch (e) {
Dojo.check("does not mutate frozen state", false, String(e));
hints: For `add`, check `some(l => l.sku === action.sku)` and either `map` or append.
Guard `remove` and `setQty` with the same `some` check and `return state`.

steps.title: Derived values, not stored values
prompt: Do not store what you can compute. Write `cartSummary(state: CartState, prices: Record<string, number>)` returning `{ count, totalCents, lines }` where `lines` is `["2 x tea = $5.00", ...]`. Unknown skus cost 0.
In React this runs during render (wrapped in `useMemo` only if it is slow).
starter: type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
function cartSummary(state: CartState, prices: Record<string, number>) {
return { count: 0, totalCents: 0, lines: [] as string[] };
solution: type Line = { sku: string; qty: number };
function cartSummary(state: CartState, prices: Record<string, number>) {
const count = state.lines.reduce((n, l) => n + l.qty, 0);
const totalCents = state.lines.reduce((t, l) => t + l.qty * (prices[l.sku] ?? 0), 0);
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.eq("summary", { count: 3, totalCents: 820, lines: ["2 x tea = $5.00", "1 x cake = $3.20"] }, cartSummary({ lines: [{ sku: "tea", qty: 2 }, { sku: "cake", qty: 1 }] }, { tea: 250, cake: 320 }));
Dojo.eq("unknown sku costs 0", { count: 1, totalCents: 0, lines: ["1 x x = $0.00"] }, cartSummary({ lines: [{ sku: "x", qty: 1 }] }, {}));
Dojo.eq("empty", { count: 0, totalCents: 0, lines: [] }, cartSummary({ lines: [] }, {}));
